thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT (P1) — GPU OOM during prefill observed across two pods in cluster-phi. Paging oncall.
Raj: got pager 2187659999 — multiple containers restarted due to OOM while handling long prefill requests from a single customer. Spinning up thread.
Mia: on it, jumping in. Which nodes? any crashloops?
Raj: pods: runtime-gen-9845 and runtime-gen-9912 on gnode-13 + gnode-14. Both restarted ~3x in last 10m. Crash loop started after a spike in long-context requests.
Anna: saw the logs; prefill length for the offending requests is ~28k tokens (customer batch of large docs). GPU memory shot up during KV cache allocation, then CUDART reports OOM -> container restart.
Raj: log snippet:
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:xxx] failed to allocate device memory: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
E runtime: prefill kv allocation failed at 0x7fdb... size=24,000,000
I containerd: Killing process 32177 (runtime-server) due to OOM
```
Mia: is this a single customer, or a pattern across customers?
Anna: so far only one tenant (tid-9987) sending huge batched uploads. But autoscaler tried to reschedule and hit the same due to affinity rules.
infra-bot: node gnode-13 shows GPU utilization spike to 98% at 02:12 UTC, then kernel reports 3 OOM kills; gnode-14 similar. No node-level OOMs, containers killed by cgroups.
Mia: immediate mitigations I can try now:
- cordon node gnode-13 and gnode-14 to stop scheduling new pods
- patch runtime deployment to cap prefill tokens per request (soft limit) via env REDWOOD_PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP=8000
- enable fallback model variant that uses quantized weights and smaller KV cache
Raj: +1 to cordon. Also we should throttle the customer's request rate from the API gateway if possible.
Customer Success: we already put them on a temporary rate limit at their org level (api key blocked for write ops). Will follow up with a customer-facing note. Need ETA for recovery.
Mia: executing cordon now and applying prefill cap as a rapid config rollout (will patch deployment). If patch fails can scale replicas=0 for the affected pool.
Anna: while cordon is in progress, I'll add a kube network policy to reroute new requests for model-gen to the fallback pool.
Ops Lead: lifecycle question — do we want to evict existing pods or let them die naturally? Evicting could cause more restarts.
Mia: don't force evict. We'll cordon and let existing pods serve until they OOM; with cap and fallback new pods should be safe.
Raj: gateway throttle applied to the tenant now. We see incoming requests drop by 92%.
Mia: patch applied: set REDWOOD_PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP=8000 and MAX_BATCH_SIZE=4 for runtime-gen pool. Rolling update started.
infra-bot: rolling update status: 2/6 pods updated, 0 failures so far. New pods are up on gnode-16 and gnode-17 (different hosts).
Anna: new pods report reduced KV allocation and stable memory. Old nodes still have one crashlooping pod each.
Mia: monitoring for 10m to confirm stability. Can someone post a short customer notice template I can approve? Customer Success?
Customer Success: drafting: "We observed increased error rates due to very large prompt ingestion from your account. We temporarily limited prefill size and rate to stabilize service. No data loss. We're working with you on a plan to support larger contexts." Will DM details.
Raj: prelim postmortem notes: root cause = unbounded prefill token size + batch of large docs from single tenant -> KV cache allocation spiking; secondary cause = pod scheduling pinned to two nodes without burst capacity.
Ops Lead: next steps: 1) make prefill token cap a platform default (8000) with org opt-out and monitoring; 2) improve gateway detection to auto-throttle extreme token sizes; 3) add node-level spread for runtime-gen pool; 4) run a chaos test for long-context prefill to validate fallback.
Mia: agreed. For this incident I'm assigning the runbook tasks: Raj = post-incident data capture (logs + request IDs), Anna = patch gateway and node spread, Ops Lead = follow up with infra for capacity increases.
oncall-bot: Incident updated: status=stabilized, severity=P1 -> P2, incident-channel linked.
Mia: closing pager handoff to next rotation @Anna in 20m once we confirm no more restarts. Leaving thread open for customer update and postmortem.
Customer Success: customer updated via email at 02:48 UTC. They acknowledged and are compiling their request patterns. Will attach their example payloads for postmortem.
Raj: saving all logs and core dumps to /var/incident/2187659999.tar.gz and will attach to the postmortem doc.
Anna: creating the postmortem draft now. We'll include exact request IDs and mitigations.
Mia: thanks team — great quick coordination. :thumbsup:
